title: Ordinary discrete actions and internal condensed actions
statement:
Fix the small coherent site of profinite sets, whose covers are finite jointly surjective families, and compatible coefficient universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $\mathcal M_R$ be its internal module category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and use the section modules of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Let $G$ be any group with underlying set in the coefficient universe, equipped with the discrete topology, and let $BG$ be the category with one object and automorphism group $G$. Write $\mathcal A_R(G)$ for the category of internal modules with natural linear $C(S,G)$-actions [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. There is an additive equivalence
$$\Phi_G:\operatorname{Fun}(BG,\mathcal M_R)\simeq\mathcal A_R(G)$$
which leaves every underlying internal module and every morphism unchanged. For an ordinary action $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal M_R}(M)$, a profinite set $S$, a continuous $g:S\to G$, and $m\in M(S)$, its action is characterized by
$$(g\cdot m)|_{S_a}=\rho(a)_{S_a}(m|_{S_a}),\qquad S_a=g^{-1}(a),\quad a\in g(S).$$
Here $g(S)$ is finite, each $S_a$ is clopen, and these inclusions form a finite covering family. The inverse equivalence takes the action of $a\in G$ to that of the constant map $S\to G$ with value $a$ on every $S$. In particular the equivalence preserves the specified underlying-module functors and trivial-action functors. This includes the trivial group, the empty test profinite set, the zero ring and the zero module.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], work with the sectionwise module sheaf of each internal module, without changing sections or morphisms. Its underlying abelian sheaf satisfies [lem-sfb-profinite-coherent-sheaf-criterion]. Consequently, for every finite disjoint clopen partition $S=\coprod_i S_i$, restriction gives a bijection $M(S)\to\prod_i M(S_i)$ of abelian groups. It is $R(S)$-linear, where $R(S)$ acts through restriction on each factor: this follows by restricting $rm$ to every $S_i$. Its inverse is therefore linear too. In particular sections are equal if their restrictions to all partition members are equal, every tuple has a unique glued section, and $M(\varnothing)=0$ (the empty product). These facts apply to every module below.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written algebraic input; finite disjoint-partition gluing; compare Mathlib/Condensed/Discrete/LocallyConstant.lean, proof sketch, and Sites/Coherent/SheafComparison.lean:236-243

proof.text: For $g:S\to G$ continuous with $G$ discrete, each fiber $S_a=g^{-1}(a)$ is open, and closed because its complement is the inverse image of the open subset $G\setminus\{a\}$. The fibers cover $S$; compactness gives finitely many fibers covering $S$, so every nonempty fiber is one of these and $g(S)$ is finite. Each clopen fiber is profinite: Hausdorffness and total disconnectedness are inherited by subspaces, and an open cover of a closed subset extends to one of $S$ by adjoining its complement, proving compactness. The inclusions are jointly surjective and hence a finite cover by [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. The same applies to common refinements $S_a\cap S_b'$ and to inverse images of fibers along arbitrary maps of profinite sets. Empty parts may be retained, since their section modules are zero by step 1.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written algebraic input; compactness and the finite clopen fiber partition

proof.text: Let $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Aut}(M)$ be the ordinary action. For $g\in C(S,G)$ define $A_S(g)m$ to be the unique section whose restriction to every $S_a$, $a\in g(S)$, is $\rho(a)_{S_a}(m|_{S_a})$, using step 1. This proves existence and the stated characterization, including uniqueness of an extension with that formula. Every $\rho(a)$ is an internal linear morphism, so these local formulas preserve sums and multiplication by $r|_{S_a}$ for $r\in R(S)$. Restriction is injective, hence $A_S(g)$ is an $R(S)$-linear endomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written algebraic input; construction and linearity of the action by the fiber formula

proof.text: The constant function with value $1$ acts identically, since its local formula is $\rho(1)=1$. For $g,h\in C(S,G)$ use the finite disjoint refinement $S_{a,b}=g^{-1}(a)\cap h^{-1}(b)$. Naturality of each internal map $\rho(a)$ shows that on this part $A_S(g)A_S(h)m$ restricts to $\rho(a)_{S_{a,b}}\rho(b)_{S_{a,b}}(m|_{S_{a,b}})=\rho(ab)_{S_{a,b}}(m|_{S_{a,b}})$. The fiber formula for $gh$, restricted further to this part, gives exactly the same expression. By step 1, $A_S(gh)=A_S(g)A_S(h)$. Thus $A_S$ is a group action; $A_S(g^{-1})$ is its inverse.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written algebraic input; identity and multiplication checked on the common fiber partition

proof.text: For a continuous map $u:T\to S$, partition $T$ by $T_a=u^{-1}(S_a)$. On $T_a$, naturality of $\rho(a)$ gives $u^*(A_S(g)m)|_{T_a}=\rho(a)_{T_a}((u^*m)|_{T_a})$. This is also the restriction of $A_T(g\circ u)(u^*m)$ by its defining formula. Equality on the partition gives $u^*A_S(g)m=A_T(g\circ u)u^*m$. Consequently the $A_S$ satisfy exactly the natural sectionwise linear action definition [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and determine an object of $\mathcal A_R(G)$. No continuity condition on a topology of $M(S)$ is being imposed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written algebraic input; naturality under every profinite test morphism

proof.text: If $f:M\to N$ is equivariant for the ordinary actions, restrict $f_S A_S(g)m$ and $A'_S(g)f_Sm$ to $S_a$. Naturality of $f$ and $f\rho(a)=\rho'(a)f$ make both restrictions $\rho'(a)_{S_a} f_{S_a}(m|_{S_a})$. By step 1 they agree. Therefore retain $f$ itself as the morphism of the extended actions. Identities and composition are retained, defining $\Phi_G$. Since addition and zero of equivariant maps are the underlying ones in [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and likewise pointwise in $\operatorname{Fun}(BG,\mathcal M_R)$, this functor is additive.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written algebraic input; extension of equivariant morphisms and additivity

proof.text: Conversely, for an object with action $A$ as in [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], set $\rho(a)_S=A_S(\operatorname{const}_S a)$. Naturality of $A$ makes this a natural sectionwise linear morphism. The equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], whose forward functor is the identity on underlying sheaves and section maps, yields the corresponding internal linear map. The group law gives $\rho(1)=1$, $\rho(ab)=\rho(a)\rho(b)$ and inverse $\rho(a^{-1})$, hence a functor from $BG$. An equivariant internal-action morphism commutes with constant actions, so retaining its underlying map defines the inverse functor $\Psi_G$, which is additive by the same underlying-map calculation.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written algebraic input; restriction to constant functions and reconstruction of the ordinary action

proof.text: Starting with $\rho$, the extension evaluated at a constant $a$ is $\rho(a)_S$ on every nonempty $S$; on the empty test both are the unique endomorphism of zero. Hence $\Psi_G\Phi_G$ is the original ordinary action. Starting with $A$, naturality along $S_a\hookrightarrow S$ gives $(A_S(g)m)|_{S_a}=A_{S_a}(\operatorname{const}_{S_a}a)(m|_{S_a})$. These are exactly the local formulas of the reconstructed extension, so uniqueness in step 1 gives $\Phi_G\Psi_G=A$. Both composites fix morphisms; the identity underlying module maps give unit and counit and their triangle identities. This proves the additive equivalence over the specified underlying-module functors.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written algebraic input; both inverse identities and equivalence coherence

proof.text: If the ordinary action is trivial, every local formula is $m|_{S_a}$, so gluing returns $m$ and the extended action is trivial. Restricting the trivial internal action to constants is also trivial; thus both specified trivial-action functors are preserved. For $G=1$ all functions are the constant identity. For the empty test set the partition is empty and the module of sections is zero by step 1. For the zero module all formulas are unique; for the zero coefficient ring every unital section module is zero because $m=1m=0m=0$. Thus none of the constructions excludes the edge cases stated in the item.
